outcome: Proportion of infants with birthweight > 4500 g
cohort: Singleton, cephalic, vaginally delivered infants born in Sweden between 1997 and 2019.
finding: The incidence of obstetric brachial plexus palsy (OBPP) in vaginally delivered infants in a cephalic presentation decreased from 1997 to 2019, despite an increase in several associated risk factors including shoulder dystocia.
mod_finding: The study focused on vaginally delivered infants, finding a decline in OBPP within this group and also noting a decrease in the rate of operative vaginal delivery over time.
birth_weight: Not specified for the overall cohort, but infants with birthweight >4500 g were a subgroup whose incidence over time was analyzed.
